failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 8 hidden cases. The docs did well in the exact areas this task needed: the Tag Processor overview says to use the HTML Processor for missing closing tags and normalized output; the HTML Processor text-extraction recipe says ordinary text means #text tokens only, not every token with modifiable text; get_modifiable_text() states #text/TITLE/TEXTAREA text is decoded while comments/raw-text sections differ; and serialize_token() explicitly documents token-by-token normalized rewrites, including wrapping selected text tokens. These passages explain why the candidates avoided matching attributes/comments, matched entity-encoded keywords, preserved split text-node behavior, and produced normalized implied closers. The main near-miss is the shared fallback explanation: all candidates call normalize($html) after a rewrite loop if get_last_error() is non-null. The docs do warn that normalize($html) starts over from the original bytes and discards emitted changes, so this is not a hallucination, but it is a contract risk for unsupported markup after earlier matches. They also did not check paused_at_incomplete_token(); for this normalized-output task the accumulated serialization omits unvisited incomplete trailing syntax, which is acceptable, but tasks requiring complete source bytes would need that check.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn that normalize($html) discards emitted rewrite output, but the candidates still treated normalize($html) ?? $html as a generic recovery path after a rewrite loop.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short decision table for rewrite-loop failure policy: strict contract returns null/empty or throws; best-effort returns accumulated output; fallback normalization deliberately discards all emitted rewrites; raw input fallback is not normalized output.

doc_gaps.problem: The relationship between processor-creation failure, unsupported-markup aborts, and normalized-output contracts is spread across multiple sections.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Cross-link the factory and normalization docs to the rewrite-loop policy, explicitly stating that normalize($html) is only a fresh normalization of original input, not recovery of a partially serialized transformation.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain that SCRIPT/STYLE/TITLE/TEXTAREA carry text on opener tokens, but this remains easy to miss when a task says ordinary text nodes only.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small token-stream example for ordinary text versus special-element opener text, showing that callers should require get_token_type() === '#text' unless they explicitly opt into those element contents.
